description: Historical price charts and news feed integration for Viper Terminal
principles: Rock-solid quality over speed - every feature must be bulletproof before moving on
Comprehensive test coverage - unit tests, integration tests, edge cases
All tests must pass before a story is marked complete
No story is done until it's documented and tested
Fail fast, fail loudly - errors should be obvious and actionable
Reuse existing patterns from MVP - consistent architecture
Performance matters - charts must render quickly even with large datasets

techStack.newsData: Yahoo Finance RSS (primary), Finnhub API (optional enhancement)

userStories.title: Historical price data service
acceptanceCriteria: Create viper/services/history_data.py (avoid confusion with history.py)
Define HistoricalData dataclass: dates, prices, volumes, highs, lows, opens, closes
Fetch data via yfinance Ticker.history() with configurable period/interval
Support periods: 1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y, 5Y, MAX
Handle invalid tickers gracefully - return HistoricalDataError
Handle empty data (new IPOs, delisted stocks)
Async wrapper to not block UI
Calculate period stats: high, low, % change, avg volume
Tests: valid fetch (mocked), all periods, empty data, invalid ticker, timeout
userStories.notes: Foundation for all chart features. yfinance already supports this via history() method.

userStories.title: Chart rendering engine
acceptanceCriteria: Create viper/widgets/chart_renderer.py
Implement BrailleChart class for high-resolution line charts
Braille patterns: 2x4 dots per character = 160x80 resolution in 80x20 chars
Support auto-scaling: normalize data to fit available height
Support auto-downsampling: reduce data points to fit width
Render Y-axis with price labels (left side)
Render X-axis with date labels (bottom)
Color support: green for uptrend, red for downtrend sections
Fallback to block characters (▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█) for simpler rendering
Tests: rendering with various data sizes, edge cases (flat line, single point)
userStories.notes: Core rendering logic. Braille gives ~8x resolution vs standard characters. This is the most complex story.

userStories.title: Chart panel widget
acceptanceCriteria: Create viper/widgets/chart_panel.py
ChartPanel widget displays historical price chart
Toggle with 'c' key (replaces quote panel when visible)
Show ticker and timeframe in header
Show period stats: high, low, % change
Loading state with spinner during data fetch
Error state when data unavailable
Empty state when no ticker selected
Responsive: adjust chart size to terminal dimensions
Tests: all display states, toggle behavior, responsive sizing
userStories.notes: Integrates chart renderer into the UI. Similar pattern to QuotePanel/InfoPanel.

userStories.title: Timeframe selection
acceptanceCriteria: Number keys 1-7 select timeframe when chart panel is visible
Visual indicator shows current timeframe (highlighted button style)
Timeframe persists until changed or ticker changes
Default to 1M on new ticker
Smooth transition: show loading while fetching new timeframe
Tests: each hotkey, visual indicator, persistence, default behavior
userStories.notes: Quick timeframe switching is essential for usability.

userStories.title: Volume chart overlay
acceptanceCriteria: Add volume bars below price chart (optional, toggle with 'v')
Volume bars use block characters (▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█)
Bars colored: green if close > open, red if close < open
Height proportional to volume (normalized to max in period)
Takes ~3 lines of vertical space
Volume stats shown: avg daily volume, volume today vs avg
Tests: volume rendering, color logic, toggle behavior
userStories.notes: Volume context helps understand price movements.

userStories.title: Crypto historical charts
acceptanceCriteria: Extend historical data service to support crypto via CoinGecko
CoinGecko market_chart endpoint: /coins/{id}/market_chart?vs_currency=usd&days=N
Map periods to days: 1W=7, 1M=30, 3M=90, 6M=180, 1Y=365, MAX=max
Handle CoinGecko rate limits (retry with backoff)
Auto-detect asset type and use appropriate data source
Tests: crypto fetch (mocked), rate limit handling, auto-detection
userStories.notes: yfinance has limited crypto history. CoinGecko provides better data for crypto.

userStories.title: News data service
acceptanceCriteria: Create viper/services/news.py
Define NewsItem dataclass: title, source, url, published_at, summary (optional)
Fetch news via Yahoo Finance RSS: https://feeds.finance.yahoo.com/rss/2.0/headline?s=TICKER
Parse RSS feed (use feedparser library)
Return list of NewsItem, sorted by recency
Handle missing/empty feeds gracefully
Handle network errors with appropriate error types
Cache results for 2 minutes (avoid repeated fetches)
Limit to 10 most recent items
Tests: valid fetch (mocked), empty feed, invalid ticker, network errors, caching
userStories.notes: Yahoo RSS is free, no API key needed. feedparser is well-maintained and handles edge cases.

userStories.title: News panel widget
acceptanceCriteria: Create viper/widgets/news_panel.py
NewsPanel widget displays news headlines for current ticker
Toggle with 'n' key
Show: headline (truncated to fit), source, relative time (2h ago, 1d ago)
j/k navigation through news items when panel focused
Visual highlight on selected item
Loading state during fetch
Empty state: 'No news available'
Auto-refresh when ticker changes
Tests: all display states, navigation, toggle, auto-refresh
userStories.notes: Similar pattern to WatchlistPanel for navigation.

userStories.title: News item expansion and browser integration
acceptanceCriteria: Enter on news item opens full article in default browser
Use Python's webbrowser.open() for cross-platform support
Alternative: 'e' key expands item inline to show summary (if available)
Expanded view shows full headline + summary in a scrollable area
Esc collapses expanded item
Status bar shows 'Opening in browser...' feedback
Tests: browser open (mocked), expansion toggle, keyboard handling
userStories.notes: Essential for actually reading the news articles.

userStories.title: Data caching layer
acceptanceCriteria: Create viper/services/cache.py
Generic cache class with TTL (time-to-live) support
Cache historical data for 5 minutes
Cache news data for 2 minutes
Cache quotes for 30 seconds (don't re-fetch on panel toggle)
Clear cache for ticker when new ticker selected
Memory-only cache (no disk persistence needed)
Thread-safe implementation
Tests: cache hit/miss, TTL expiration, clearing, thread safety
userStories.notes: Reduces API calls and improves responsiveness. Can be implemented early and used by all services.

userStories.title: Help screen updates
acceptanceCriteria: Update HelpScreen with new keybindings: c (chart), n (news), v (volume), 1-7 (timeframes)
Add CHARTS section describing chart features
Add NEWS section describing news features
Update FEATURES section with new capabilities
Tests: help screen content includes new sections
userStories.notes: Documentation is part of the feature.

userStories.title: Configuration extensions
acceptanceCriteria: Add config options: default_chart_timeframe, news_enabled, volume_enabled
Add config option: chart_style ('braille' or 'block')
Add config option: news_max_items (default 10)
Validate new config options with sensible defaults
Tests: new config options load correctly, validation, defaults

brailleCharting.description: Braille patterns allow 2x4 dots per character, giving much higher resolution than standard characters
algorithm: 1. Normalize data to 0-1 range based on min/max
2. For each column, determine which of 4 vertical dots should be filled
3. Combine adjacent columns (2 cols = 1 braille char with 2x4 dots)
4. Map dot pattern to Unicode braille character
5. Apply colors based on trend direction

rssFeeds.notes: Yahoo is more finance-focused, Google is broader but may have more noise

performanceConsiderations: Downsample historical data before rendering (max ~200 points for 80-col terminal)
Cache aggressively to avoid repeated API calls
Render charts incrementally if data is very large
Use async workers for all data fetching
